name: Three Flashes
explanation: This is the strict version of SC 2.3.1, with the below-threshold exception removed entirely. At Level A, a flash is still allowed if it's small or low-contrast enough to fall below the general and red flash thresholds. At this AAA level, nothing may flash more than three times in any one-second period, no matter how small or subtle the flash is. This removes the judgment call of measuring flash size and contrast against a threshold. If it flashes more than three times a second, it fails, regardless of scale.
whoItAffects: SC 2.3.1's threshold-based rule already protects people with photosensitive epilepsy in most cases. But the below-threshold exception exists for a reason. Very small or low-contrast flashing still carries some risk of triggering a seizure, just a much lower one. This stricter AAA criterion removes that remaining risk for the most sensitive people. It bans rapid flashing outright, instead of allowing it below a calculated threshold.
howToTest: Watch every animated or flashing element on the page, no matter how small, for a full second at a time. Count how many times it flashes. Unlike SC 2.3.1, don't stop to measure whether it's below a size or contrast threshold. At this AAA level, any element flashing more than three times per second fails outright, no matter how minor it looks.

check.question: A small notification icon in the corner of the page pulses 5 times per second, but it's tiny and low-contrast enough that it falls below the general flash threshold used in SC 2.3.1. Does this pass the stricter SC 2.3.2 Three Flashes?
choices: Yes, because falling below the general flash threshold satisfies both criteria
No, because SC 2.3.2 has no below-threshold exception, so any flash rate over three per second fails regardless of size
Yes, because notification icons are exempt from flash criteria
It depends only on whether the icon is decorative
